Looking for a school place in Year R or Year 3 for September 2026 or an in year application? Call on 01730 829213 to book a visit.
Red warning for extreme heat has been extended to Friday at 9pm. The school will be closed from 1pm Friday 26th June for half a day
Our Christian Values of Respect, Courage and Creativity are at the heart of our school. They are reflected in both our high expectations for all and our nurturing approach to educating young people.
Children at West Meon Primary develop self-awareness and confidence in an environment where they feel safe, happy and valued; where they are encouraged to develop their skills, talents, and a life-long love of learning in an inclusive, nurturing setting.
Take a look at our Weekly Round Up HERE
Today, the children of West Meon School were sadly unable to make their planned trip to West Wittering beach due to the extreme heat. 🌡️ But not to worry, we decided that if we couldn’t go to the beach, we would bring the beach to us!
Our playground was transformed into a seaside paradise, complete with paddling pools, sand, and plenty of refreshing ice lollies. 🍦💦 The children had an amazing time splashing in the water, building in the sand, fishing in rock pools, blowing bubbles, and enjoying the chance to cool off with their friends.
It may not have been the trip we planned, but it certainly turned into a day full of laughter, fun, and unforgettable summer memories. 😊
Well done to all the children for making the most of the day, and thank you to everyone who helped create such a special experience! 🌊💛

🐣 Exciting News from Our School! 🐣
We are thrilled to be hosting a wonderful egg‑to‑chick experience right here at school! Our pupils have been learning all about the life cycle of a chicken — from egg, to hatching, to fluffy chick — and it’s been amazing to watch this process up close.
🥚➡️🐥 We’re delighted to share that six eggs have successfully hatched, and the chicks are doing well!
If anyone is interested, the chicks will be available for sale at £5 per chick. Please get in touch if you’d like more information or would like to give one of these lovely chicks a new home.
Yesterday, Thursday 12th March, Foxes Class had an amazing day out in London as part of their learning about the Egyptians and their way of life! 🇪🇬✨
The journey itself was an adventure — they travelled by minibus, overhead train and even the Tube! The excitement was sky‑high, especially because some children had never been on the Tube before. Their faces lit up as the train whooshed through the tunnels! 🚇💙
On the way into London, the children loved spotting all the famous tourist sights from the train — a little sightseeing tour before the real learning even began! 🏙️👀
It was a big day too: they set off at 8am and didn’t arrive back until just after 5pm. But despite the long journey, everyone agreed it was a fantastic day filled with fun, learning, and unforgettable moments. 🎒📚
A huge well done to Foxes Class for being such brilliant explorers! 🦊✨
🌟 Hedgehogs & Hoglets’ Marwell Adventure! 🌟
On Wednesday 11th March, our Hedgehogs and Hoglets had an absolutely fantastic day out at Marwell Zoo! 🦓🦒🐅
The children were thrilled to discover so many amazing animals — from graceful giraffes and cheeky meerkats to roaring big cats and waddling penguins. Their excitement grew with every new creature they spotted!
One of the highlights of the day was hopping aboard the Marwell train, chugging around the zoo and spotting even more animals along the way. 🚂🐾 Laughter, curiosity, and big smiles filled the whole journey.
We’re so proud of how enthusiastic, kind, and curious the children were throughout the whole trip. They all had a brilliant time exploring, learning, and enjoying the adventure together. 💛

pageCache.pageTitle: Strategic responsibilities | West Meon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Strategic responsibilities
Governing bodies work closely with headteachers and senior leaders. Headteachers are responsible for operations and while the governing body stays strategic. As such, governors are responsible for:
· determining mission, values and long-term ambitious vision
· deciding the principles that guide school policies and approving key policies
· working with senior leaders to develop a strategy for achieving the vision
· ensuring that parents, pupils, staff and the wider community are involved, consulted and informed as appropriate
· ensuring that all pupils have access to a broad and balanced curriculum such that pupils are well prepared for the next stage of their education and adult life
· setting the school’s budget and ensuring it is managed effectively together with premises and other resources
· agreeing the school’s staffing structure and keeping it under review to ensure it supports delivery of the strategy
· ensuring robust risk management procedures are in place and that risk control measures are appropriate and effective
West Meon CofE Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Behaviour Principles | West Meon CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Behaviour Principles
Statement of Behaviour Principles
The Education and Inspectors Act 2006 and DfE guidance (Behaviour in Schools, 2012) requires Governors to produce and frequently review a written statement of general behaviour principles to guide the Headteacher in determining measures to promote good behaviour and discipline amongst pupils.
The purpose of this statement is to give guidance to the Headteacher in drawing up the Behaviour Policy by stating the principles that Governors expect to be followed.
1. Every pupil understands they have the right to feel safe, valued and respected, and learn free from the disruption of others
2. All current and prospective pupils, staff and visitors are free from any form of discrimination
3. Staff, volunteers, and Governors set an excellent example to pupils at all times
4. Rewards, sanctions and reasonable force are used consistently by staff, in line with the behaviour policy
5. The behaviour policy is understood by pupils and staff
6. The exclusions policy explains that exclusions will only be used as a last resort, and outlines the processes involved in permanent and fixed-term exclusions
7. Pupils are helped to take responsibility for their actions
8. Families are involved in behaviour incidents to foster good relationships between the school and pupils’ home life
9. The governing board emphasises that violence or threatening behaviour will not be tolerated in any circumstances.
This written statement of behaviour principles is reviewed and approved by the full governing board every year.
West Meon CofE Primary School

Dunhurst U11 Football Tournament
On Wednesday 22nd December some of our Year 5 & 6 children joined other schools at Dunhurst School for a football tournament. We were delighted that we could take part once again in inter schools sports, something that has been put on hold for over 18 months.
Every child did really well and thoroughly enjoyed the afternoon. Long may it last!
